e: An Aurora Serverless cluster scales capacity down (even pausing) when developers aren't working and charges only for capacity used, and a Service Catalog product lets developers self-provision limited-size databases. Always-on Aurora instances or manual start/stop processes cost more or need extra management.

Amazon EFS is a shared file system that every EC2 instance across Availability Zones can mount, so content changes are visible to all instances immediately with the least lag. Hourly S3 sync, EBS snapshots, or copying from the newest instance all introduce delay or inconsistency.

Amazon GuardDuty continuously detects suspicious activity and threats; EventBridge can filter its findings and invoke Lambda to update AWS WAF rules automatically, giving automated detection and response. Firewall Manager, Inspector, and Macie aren't threat detection services of this kind.

IAM database authentication for Aurora lets applications obtain short-lived authentication tokens using the instance's IAM role, so there are no static database credentials to store or rotate, and it's straightforward to configure from CloudFormation. IAM users can't be attached to EC2 instances, and stored passwords are static.

CloudFront requires certificates from ACM in us-east-1, and public ACM certificates are free (private certificates from ACM Private CA cost extra and aren't used for public distributions), so a public certificate in us-east-1 avoids additional cost.

A presigned URL grants time-limited access (set to 7 days) to just that one S3 object without creating users or making the bucket public, with little operational effort. Public buckets, websites, or IAM users with keys over-expose data or need more management.

A cluster placement group packs instances close together within an Availability Zone, giving low latency and high network throughput for tightly coupled node-to-node HPC communication. Dedicated tenancy, Spot, and capacity reservations don't affect network placement.

Maximum resiliency means redundant connections at each data center that terminate at separate Direct Connect locations on separate devices, so no single device, connection, or location failure breaks connectivity. The other options share a device, location, or only one site's redundancy.

From the management account, the Trusted Advisor organizational view gives consolidated recommendations for all member accounts, and the RDS Reserved Instance Optimization check finds highly utilized On-Demand DB instances that would be cheaper as Reserved Instances. Idle DB instance and compute optimization checks don't apply to busy Oracle instances.

An S3 gateway endpoint in the VPC with a route table entry keeps S3 traffic on the AWS network and has no hourly or data processing charges, which minimizes data transfer cost for large files. NAT gateways and interface endpoints charge for hours and data processed.

RDS for MySQL on Provisioned IOPS SSD storage is built for write-heavy, I/O-intensive workloads, with IOPS that can be monitored in CloudWatch and adjusted. A cache helps reads rather than writes, and DocumentDB or EFS are the wrong data stores.

To keep third parties from seeing the data before it's sent to AWS, the application must encrypt the files itself (client-side encryption) with a key managed in KMS before uploading. S3 server-side encryption only encrypts after the data arrives, and S3 doesn't provide a client-side encryption setting.
RDS automated backups already take a daily backup; simply set the backup retention period to 30 days. No Lambda, Systems Manager, or manual snapshots are needed.

Adding an Aurora Replica to the existing cluster offloads reads to the reader endpoint while writes go to the cluster (writer) endpoint, improving write performance at low cost with no data copying. DAX is for DynamoDB, and a second cluster or Redshift adds cost and complexity.

Kinesis Data Firehose is a serverless, scalable ingestion service for near-real-time data, and ECS on Fargate runs the 30-minute processing job serverlessly without the 15-minute Lambda limit. EC2 Auto Scaling isn't serverless, and DMS isn't for streaming ingestion.

An S3 gateway VPC endpoint with a route in the VPC route table keeps traffic between the instances and S3 on the AWS network, not the public internet. S3 buckets can't be deployed inside a VPC or be NLB targets, and Direct Connect isn't for VPC-to-S3 traffic.

AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes EBS volumes' configuration and utilization and recommends optimizations, including estimated monthly savings. Inspector, Systems Manager, and CloudWatch don't provide cost-saving recommendations for EBS.

S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide, cross-Region metrics and recommendations, including the number of buckets without versioning enabled. Access Analyzer reports on access, and Multi-Region Access Points route requests. Note: the PDF text for option A is missing; B is the correct choice among the others.

An SQS FIFO queue guarantees exactly-once processing and ordering, buffers traffic surges, and a Lambda function consumer scales automatically. SNS standard topics can deliver duplicates, and AppFlow and X-Ray aren't order-processing queues.

Create an IAM role in the Production account whose trust policy names the Development account, then allow developers there to assume it; adding more beta-phase developers just means granting them permission to assume the role. A role in Development can't grant access to Production resources.

Cognito provides serverless authentication that scales from a small user base to many users, Lambda@Edge handles authorization at CloudFront edge locations for low latency, and CloudFront serves the web application globally. Directory Service, ALB, Beanstalk, or S3 Transfer Acceleration don't provide this serverless global design.

With AWS Organizations, a service control policy that denies launching large instance types applied to the accounts (or OUs) enforces the restriction across all accounts centrally, with the least overhead. IAM policies or roles in each account must be managed individually, and RAM doesn't restrict launches.

Systems Manager Patch Manager automates OS inventory and patching for both Windows and Linux instances, and Amazon Inspector scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities and produces findings and reports for monthly reviews. Security Hub aggregates but doesn't scan, and Config, Shield, or GuardDuty don't patch or assess vulnerabilities.

A warm standby in the DR Region (Auto Scaling group and ELB already running) with a DynamoDB global table keeps data replicated, and DNS failover (Route 53 health checks) switches traffic automatically, giving the least downtime. Launching resources with CloudFormation when needed or waiting on a 10-minute alarm adds downtime.

An S3 gateway endpoint lets instances in private subnets reach S3 over the AWS network, not the public internet, and it costs nothing. NAT gateways and interface endpoints add hourly and data charges, and Storage Gateway is for hybrid access.
